en: To mistakenly think that one person or thing is another; or to regard something as being a particular thing.
ex: I took him for a teacher, but he's a student.
我把他當成老師，其實他是學生。

en: To chase someone or something; or to try to get or achieve something.
ex: The police went after the robber.
警察追捕搶匪。

en: To become less strong or severe; or to stop for a short time.
ex: The rain let up in the afternoon.
下午雨勢減弱了。

en: To happen, especially in a planned way; or to occur.
ex: The ceremony will take place on Sunday.
典禮將於週日舉行。

en: To stop being popular or fashionable.
ex: That style fell out of fashion years ago.
那種款式多年前就過時了。

en: To become friends again after a quarrel.
ex: She finally made up with her best friend.
她終於與最好的朋友和好了。

en: To remain outside or away from home, especially at night.
ex: The teenagers stayed out until midnight.
青少年們在外面待到午夜。

en: To make progress; or to arrive; or to come with someone.
ex: How's your new project coming along?
你的新專案進展如何？

en: To redo or change something; or to transfer ownership of something.
ex: They made over the old kitchen completely.
他們把舊廚房完全改造了一番。

en: To have a better opinion of someone because of something they did.
ph: think all the better of him
col: think all the better of her for it
ex: I think all the better of her for admitting her mistake.
她承認錯誤，我反而更敬重她。

en: To cancel an event or plan that was arranged.
ex: The match was called off because of rain.
比賽因雨取消了。

en: To look at something that is below you; or to lower your eyes.
ex: She looked down at her shoes and smiled.
她低頭看著鞋子，微微一笑。

en: To have an idea or memory in your mind; or to consider someone or something.
ex: I can't think of her name right now.
我現在想不起她的名字。

en: To be good for someone or to benefit them.
ex: A walk will do you good.
散散步對你有好處。

en: To use someone's feelings or weaknesses to get what you want; or to continue playing.
ex: The advertisers play on people's fears.
廣告商利用人們的恐懼心理。

en: To not pay attention to someone or something.
ph: take no notice of the warning
col: take no notice of the rules
ex: He took no notice of her advice.
他完全沒理會她的忠告。

en: To explode; or to become very angry; or to fill something with air; or to enlarge a photograph.
ex: The bomb blew up the old building.
炸彈炸毀了那棟舊建築。

en: To stop doing something; or to not include someone or something.
ex: Let's begin where we left off yesterday.
我們從昨天停下來的地方開始吧。

en: To throw something back to the person or place it came from; or to delay or set back.
ex: He threw the ball back to me.
他把球丟回給我。

en: To return to a place; or to recover something you lost or lent.
ex: When did you get back from Japan?
你什麼時候從日本回來的？

en: To grab something suddenly and hold it firmly; or to manage to obtain something.
ex: He caught hold of the branch and pulled himself up.
他抓住樹枝把自己拉上去。

en: To reject an offer or request; or to reduce the volume, heat or brightness of something.
ex: She turned down the job offer.
她拒絕了那份工作邀請。

en: To take a shorter way by going across something rather than around it; or to affect different groups.
ex: We cut across the park to save time.
我們抄近路穿過公園以節省時間。

en: To steal something and escape with it.
ex: The thieves made away with a lot of jewelry.
小偷偷走了大量珠寶。

en: To solve a problem; or to develop in a satisfactory way; or to exercise; or to calculate something.
ex: I'm sure everything will work out fine.
我相信一切都會順利解決。

en: To fail to do what you promised to do.
ex: He never breaks his word.
他從不食言。

en: To stop holding someone or something; or to stop having feelings of anger or sadness.
ex: Please let go of my hand.
請放開我的手。

en: To stop a machine, light or tap from working; or to make someone lose interest.
ex: Please turn off the lights when you leave.
離開時請關燈。

en: To slowly stop moving.
col: draw to a halt at the gate
ex: The train drew to a halt at the station.
火車緩緩停在車站。

en: To stop holding something; or to free a person or animal; or to dismiss someone from a job.
ex: The company let go of fifty workers.
公司解僱了五十名員工。

en: To take the place of someone or something; or to use one thing instead of another.
ex: Honey can substitute for sugar in this recipe.
這個食譜中蜂蜜可以代替糖。

en: To behave badly or to make a mistake.
ex: He knew he had done wrong and apologized.
他知道自己做錯了，並道了歉。

en: To stay quiet and say nothing.
ex: Please keep silence in the library.
請在圖書館保持安靜。

en: To turn on a light or machine by pressing a switch.
ex: Switch on the lamp, please.
請把燈打開。

en: To enter a place or vehicle; or to arrive; or to be admitted to a school or organization.
ex: The train gets in at seven o'clock.
火車七點進站。

en: To forget to take something with you; or to go faster than someone and leave them behind.
ex: I left my umbrella behind on the bus.
我把雨傘遺落在公車上了。

en: To get rid of something you do not want; or to reject a plan or proposal; or to force someone to leave.
ex: The judge threw out the case.
法官駁回了這個案子。

en: To compare two things and show how they are similar or different.
ex: The writer draws a comparison between the two cities.
作者將兩座城市做了比較。

en: Using hands, not machines; or delivered personally and not by post.
ex: These cookies were made by hand.
這些餅乾是手工製作的。

en: To move apart over a wide area; or to stretch something out so that it covers more space.
ex: The searchers spread out across the forest.
搜救人員在森林裡散開搜尋。
